units.zh: 少苦心為學，以明經調補華州參軍，拔萃登科，授鄠縣尉。
units.en: In his youth he applied himself rigorously to learning. He passed the classics examination and was appointed aide in Huazhou. After winning selection in the superior examination he was made assistant magistrate of E County.
units.literal: In youth he painstakingly studied; through the classics examination he was appointed Huazhou aide; selected in the superior examination and passed; granted Assistant Magistrate of E County.

units.zh: 周歷臺省，由左司郎中出為常州刺史。
units.en: He served in various posts in the Secretariat and Chancellery, and left the capital from his post as Director in the Left Bureau to become prefect of Changzhou.
units.literal: He passed through the Secretariat and Chancellery offices; from Director in the Left Bureau he went out as Prefect of Changzhou.

units.zh: 逾年，召為給事中，出為湖南觀察使，銳於為理。
units.en: A year later he was recalled to serve as a Supervising Secretariat Drafter, then sent out as commissioner of Hunan, where he governed with sharp efficiency.
units.literal: After a year he was summoned as Supervising Secretary, sent out as Hunan Observation Commissioner; he was keen on governance.

units.zh: 五年，改江西觀察使，加檢校散騎常侍、兼御史大夫。
units.en: In his fifth year he was transferred to Jiangxi as observation commissioner, with the additional titles of Acting Regular Palace Attendant and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: In the fifth year he was changed to Jiangxi Observation Commissioner, with additional Acting Regular Palace Attendant and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 巽持下以法，吏不敢欺，而動必察之。
units.en: Li Xun governed his subordinates strictly by law. Clerks did not dare cheat him—and he scrutinized every move they made.
units.literal: Xun held subordinates by law; clerks did not dare deceive, yet every movement he surely investigated.

units.zh: 順宗即位，入為兵部侍郎。
units.en: When Emperor Shunzong came to the throne, Li Xun was brought back to serve as Vice Minister of Military Affairs.
units.literal: When Shunzong took the throne, he entered the capital as Vice Minister of Military Affairs.

units.zh: 司徒杜佑判度支鹽鐵轉運使，以巽幹治，奏為副使。
units.en: Situ Du You headed the finance, salt, iron, and transport commission. Impressed by Li Xun's administrative skill, he recommended him as deputy commissioner.
units.literal: Situ Du You presided over finance, salt, iron, and transport; because Xun was capable in administration, he memorialized him as vice commissioner.

units.zh: 佑辭重位，巽遂專領度支鹽鐵使。
units.en: When Du You stepped down from the heavy office, Li Xun took sole charge of the finance and salt commission.
units.literal: You declined the heavy post; Xun then solely headed the Finance and Salt Commissioner.

units.zh: 榷筦之法，號為難重，唯大歷中僕射劉晏雅得其術，賦入豐羨。
units.en: The state monopoly system was notoriously difficult to manage. Only in the Dali era had Vice Director Liu Yan truly mastered it, yielding abundant revenue.
units.literal: The monopoly-and-control laws were called difficult and heavy; only in the Dali era Vice Director Liu Yan elegantly mastered their technique, and tax revenue was abundant.

units.zh: 巽掌使一年，征課所入，類晏之多歲，明年過之，又一年加一百八十萬貫。
units.en: In his first year in office Li Xun's tax collections matched Liu Yan's best years. The next year he exceeded that total, and in the following year he added another 1.8 million strings of cash.
units.literal: Xun held the commission one year; revenue collected matched Yan's many plentiful years; the next year surpassed it; in another year he added one million eight hundred thousand strings.

units.zh: 舊制，每歲運江淮米五十萬斛抵河陰，久不盈其數，唯巽三年登焉。
units.en: By regulation five hundred thousand shi of Jiang-Huai grain were shipped each year to Heyin, a quota long unmet—until Li Xun fulfilled it three years running.
units.literal: By old regulation, each year five hundred thousand shi of Jiang-Huai rice were transported to Heyin; for a long time the quota was not filled; only Xun in three years achieved it.

units.zh: 遷兵部尚書，明年改吏部尚書，使任如故。
units.en: He was promoted to Minister of Military Affairs, and the following year transferred to Minister of Personnel while retaining his commission unchanged.
units.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Military Affairs; the next year changed to Minister of Personnel; his commissioner duties remained as before.

units.zh: 巽精於吏職，蓋性使然也。
units.en: Li Xun excelled at bureaucratic work—it was simply in his nature.
units.literal: Xun was expert in administrative duties—probably his nature was such.

units.zh: 雖在私家，亦置案牘簿書，勾檢如公署焉。
units.en: Even at home he kept files and ledgers, auditing accounts as though he were still in a government office.
units.literal: Even in private life he also set out dossiers and ledgers, checking accounts like a public office.

units.zh: 人吏有過，絲毫無所貸，雖在千里外，其恐栗如在巽前。
units.en: He showed subordinates no mercy whatever for any fault. Even a thousand li away they trembled as though he were standing over them.
units.literal: When men and clerks had faults, not the slightest was forgiven; even a thousand li away, they trembled in fear as if before Xun.

units.zh: 初，程異附王叔文貶竄，巽知其吏才明辯，奏而用之，憲宗不違其請。
units.en: Cheng Yi had earlier been exiled for siding with Wang Shuwen, but Li Xun recognized his talent for clear, forceful administration and recommended him for office. Emperor Xianzong granted the request.
units.literal: At first Cheng Yi, having attached himself to Wang Shuwen, was exiled; Xun knew his clerical talent was clear and eloquent, memorialized and used him; Xianzong did not refuse his request.

units.zh: 異勾檢簿籍，又精於巽，故課最加衍，亦異之助焉。
units.en: Cheng Yi audited the books with even greater skill than Li Xun himself, so revenue totals kept climbing—with Cheng Yi's help.
units.literal: Yi checked ledgers and account books, and was even more expert than Xun; therefore assessment yields increased and expanded—also Yi's assistance.

units.zh: 巽為吏部尚書，臥疾，郎官相率省問，巽初不言其病，與之考校程課，商略功利，至其夕而卒。
units.en: While serving as Minister of Personnel, Li Xun fell ill. When bureau directors came in succession to visit, he at first said nothing of his illness and instead reviewed schedules and quotas with them, discussing business until he died that evening.
units.literal: Xun was Minister of Personnel, ill abed; bureau directors successively came to inquire; Xun at first did not speak of his illness, and with them examined schedules and quotas, discussed profit and utility—by that evening he died.

units.zh: 然性強很狡惡，忌刻頗甚，乘德宗之怒，謀殺竇參，物論冤之。
units.en: Yet he was by nature stubborn, ruthless, and deeply jealous. Exploiting Emperor Dezong's wrath he engineered the death of Dou Can—a killing widely regarded as unjust.
units.literal: Yet his nature was obstinate, cunning, and wicked; his jealousy and harshness were quite severe; riding Dezong's anger, he plotted to kill Dou Can—public opinion deemed it a wrongful death.

units.zh: 初，參為宰相，不悅於巽，自左司郎中出為常州刺史，仍促其行。
units.en: Earlier, when Dou Can was chancellor, Li Xun had fallen out of his favor. Can had him transferred from Director in the Left Bureau to prefect of Changzhou and pressed him to leave at once.
units.literal: At first when Can was chancellor, displeased with Xun, from Director in the Left Bureau he was sent out as Prefect of Changzhou, and his departure was still hurried.

units.zh: 不數月，參貶郴州司馬。
units.en: Within months Dou Can himself was demoted to military aide at Chenzhou.
units.literal: Within not many months Can was demoted to Military Aide of Chenzhou.

units.zh: 久之，巽自給事中為湖南觀察使，郴即屬郡也。
units.en: Later, after Li Xun had risen from Supervising Secretariat Drafter to Hunan observation commissioner, Chenzhou fell under his jurisdiction.
units.literal: After a long time, Xun went from Supervising Secretary to Hunan Observation Commissioner—Chenzhou was precisely a subordinate prefecture.

units.zh: 宣武軍節度使劉士寧以擅襲父任，物議不可，朝廷不得已而授之。
units.en: Liu Shining of Xuanwu Circuit had seized his father's command without authorization—a move widely condemned, yet the court had no choice but to confirm the appointment.
units.literal: Xuanwu Circuit Military Governor Liu Shining, for seizing his father's post on his own authority, was unacceptable in public opinion; the court had no choice but to appoint him.

units.zh: 及參之貶，士寧嘗以絹數千匹賂參，巽在湖南具奏其事，言參與籓鎮交通，德宗怒，遂賜參死，議者冤之。
units.en: When Dou Can was demoted, Liu Shining had once given him several thousand bolts of silk as a bribe. Reporting from Hunan, Li Xun laid out the full story, accusing Can of trafficking with frontier military governors. Emperor Dezong was enraged and ordered Dou Can executed—a death many considered a miscarriage of justice.
units.literal: When Can was demoted, Shining had once bribed Can with several thousand bolts of silk; Xun in Hunan fully memorialized this matter, saying Can communicated with military governors; Dezong was angry, and ordered Can's death; critics deemed it wrongful.

units.zh: 巽廉察江西，徇喜怒之情，而無罪被戮者多矣。
units.en: During his inspection tour in Jiangxi, Li Xun indulged his passions—and many innocent people were put to death.
units.literal: Xun as investigating commissioner in Jiangxi indulged feelings of favor and anger, and many who were guiltless were executed.

units.zh: 元和四年四月卒，時年七十一，贈尚書左僕射。
units.en: He died in the fourth month of 809, aged seventy-one, and was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
units.literal: Fourth month, fourth year of Yuanhe, he died, age seventy-one; posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 史臣曰：歷代操利柄為國計者，莫不損下益上，危人自安，變法以弄權，斂怨以構禍，皆有之矣。
units.en: The historian writes: Throughout history, those who held the reins of fiscal power in service of state finance have invariably enriched the throne at the people's expense, endangered others to save themselves, changed the laws to play politics, and stockpiled resentments that bred disaster—all of this has happened before.
units.literal: The historian says: In every age those who grasped the profit lever for state planning, without exception harmed the lower to benefit the upper, endangered others to secure themselves, changed laws to wield power, and gathered resentments to bring on calamity—all have had these.

units.zh: 如劉晏通擁滯，任才能，富其國而不勞於民，儉於家而利於眾。
units.en: Liu Yan was different: he cleared bottlenecks, put talent to use, enriched the state without overburdening the people, kept his household frugal, and brought benefit to all.
units.literal: Such as Liu Yan, who cleared congestion, employed talent and ability, enriched the state without burdening the people, was frugal in his household and beneficial to the multitude.

units.zh: 或問曰：鄭子產吏不能欺，宓子賤吏不忍欺，西門豹吏不敢欺。
units.en: One might ask: "With Zichan of Zheng, clerks could not cheat him; with Master Fu Ziqian, they could not bear to cheat him; with Ximen Bao, they did not dare cheat him."
units.literal: Someone asked: "Zi Chan of Zheng—clerks could not deceive him; Mi Zi Jian—clerks could not bear to deceive him; Xi Men Bao—clerks did not dare deceive him."

units.zh: 三子者，古之賢人也，吏皆懷其欺而不能、不忍、不敢也。
units.en: These three were sages of old. Their clerks may have wished to cheat them, but found themselves unable, unwilling, or too afraid.
units.literal: These three men were worthy men of antiquity; clerks all harbored deception but could not, could not bear to, and did not dare.

units.zh: 晏之吏，遠近自不欺者何也？
units.en: Why was it that Liu Yan's subordinates, near and far, simply did not cheat?
units.literal: Yan's clerks, near and far, naturally did not deceive—why?

units.zh: 答曰：蓋任其才而得其人也。
units.en: The answer: because he put the right people in the right roles and let them apply their talents.
units.literal: The answer: Probably because he employed their talents and obtained the right men.

units.zh: 晏歿，故吏二十余年繼掌財賦，不其是哉！
units.en: After Liu Yan's death, his former subordinates continued to manage the treasury for more than twenty years—is that not proof enough?
units.literal: When Yan died, his former clerks for more than twenty years successively managed finance and taxation—is this not proof!

units.zh: 《史記貨殖》云：「平糶齊物，關市不乏，治國之道也。」
units.en: The "Wealth and Profit" chapter of the Records of the Historian says, "Regulating grain prices to stabilize goods, keeping markets and frontier passes supplied—this is the art of governing."
units.literal: The "Wealth and Profit" chapter of the Records of the Historian says: "Evening out grain purchases to equalize goods, markets and passes not lacking—this is the way of governing a state."

units.zh: 晏治天下，無甚貴甚賤之物，泛言治國者，其可及乎！
units.en: Under Liu Yan's administration the realm saw neither ruinously high nor ruinously low prices. How many who speak of governing a nation can match that?
units.literal: Yan governed the realm; there were no extremely expensive or extremely cheap goods; speaking broadly of those who govern states, can they reach this!

units.zh: 舉真卿才，忠也，減王縉罪，正也，忠正之道，復出於人，嗚呼！
units.en: To recommend Yan Zhenqing showed loyalty; to lighten Wang Jin's punishment showed integrity. The virtues of loyalty and righteousness lived again in a single man—alas!
units.literal: Recommending Zhenqing's talent was loyalty; reducing Wang Jin's punishment was righteousness; the way of loyalty and righteousness again emerged in a person—alas!

units.zh: 本秀於林，風必摧之，常袞見忌於前，楊炎致冤於後，可為長嘆息矣！
units.en: A tree that stands above the forest is sure to be broken by the wind. Chang Gun resented him first; Yang Yan engineered his ruin afterward—enough to draw a long sigh.
units.literal: Timber outstanding in the forest—wind is sure to break it; Chang Gun envied him earlier; Yang Yan brought wrongful death later—one can only sigh long!

units.zh: 時譏有口者以利啖之，茍不塞讒口，何以持重權？
units.en: At the time, critics with wagging tongues were bought off with profit. Unless you silenced those tongues, how could you hold real power?
units.literal: At the time slanderers with mouths were fed with profit; if one does not stop slanderous mouths, how can one hold heavy power?

units.zh: 即無以展其才，濟其國矣。
units.en: Without that, there was no way to deploy one's abilities or serve the nation.
units.literal: Then there is no way to display one's talent and save the state.

units.zh: 是其術也，又何譏焉。
units.en: That was his approach—and what is there to condemn in it?
units.literal: This was his method—what is there to slander?

units.zh: 第五琦促辦應卒，民不加賦，而國豐饒，亦庶幾矣。
units.en: Fifth Qi mobilized resources swiftly in crisis without raising taxes on the people, and the treasury still grew flush—a feat nearly as admirable.
units.literal: Fifth Qi rushed preparations to meet emergencies; the people were not increased in taxes, yet the state was abundant—this too nearly succeeds.

units.zh: 然鑄錢變法，物貴身危，其何陋哉！
units.en: Yet his recoinage and legal tinkering drove up prices and put his own life at risk—how crude!
units.literal: Yet casting coins and changing laws made goods expensive and himself endangered—how base!

units.zh: 凡利國者，農商之外，不可為也。
units.en: As a rule, anything that enriches the state beyond agriculture and commerce should not be attempted.
units.literal: Generally what benefits the state—outside agriculture and commerce—cannot be done.

units.zh: 宏、滂爭權樹黨，皆非令人。
units.en: Ban Hong and Zhang Pang schemed for power and built factions—neither was a man one could respect.
units.literal: Hong and Pang fought for power and built factions—neither was a man to be admired.

units.zh: 紹之謹密幹事，巽之皦察精辨，亦足可稱。
units.en: Wang Shao's caution and efficiency, Li Xun's sharp-eyed precision—these too deserve recognition.
units.literal: Shao's discretion in handling affairs, Xun's clear scrutiny and precise discernment—also sufficient to praise.

units.zh: 贊曰：豐財忠良，晏道為長。
units.en: In praise: Enriching the treasury through loyal service—Liu Yan's way stands foremost.
units.literal: Eulogy: Abundant wealth and loyal integrity—Yan's way is foremost.

units.zh: 琦、宏、滂、巽，鹹以利彰。
units.en: Fifth Qi, Ban Hong, Zhang Pang, and Li Xun—all won fame through fiscal mastery.
units.literal: Qi, Hong, Pang, and Xun—all alike were famed through profit.

units.zh: 三年八月，代王縉為東都留守，充河南、淮西、山南東道副元帥，平章事如故。
units.en: In the eighth month of the third year, he replaced Wang Jin as guardian of the eastern capital, deputy commander of Henan, Huaixi, and Shannan East, while retaining his grand councilorship.
units.literal: In the eighth month of the third year, he replaced Wang Jin as guardian of the eastern capital, served as deputy commander of Henan, Huaixi, and Shannan East circuits, and remained grand councilor as before.

units.zh: 竇參當國，欲抑為刺史，帝不許。
units.en: While Dou Can held power he tried to have Jing reduced to a prefect, but the emperor refused.
units.literal: When Dou Can controlled the state he wished to demote [Jing] to prefect; the emperor did not permit it.

units.zh: 貞元中，鹹安公主降回紇，詔關播為使，而憬以御史中丞副之。
units.en: During the Zhenyuan period Princess Xian'an was married to the Uighurs. The emperor ordered Guan Bo as envoy, with Jing serving as deputy in the rank of Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: In the Zhenyuan period Princess Xian'an was married to the Uighurs; the emperor ordered Guan Bo as envoy, with Jing as deputy in the rank of Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 參罷，進中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，與陸贄同輔政。
units.en: After Can was dismissed, Jing was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-equal Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, sharing governance with Lu Zhi.
units.literal: When Can was dismissed, [Jing] was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-equal Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, assisting in governance together with Lu Zhi.

units.zh: 崔寧，本貝州安平人，後徙衛州。
units.en: Cui Ning was originally from Anping in Beizhou and later moved to Weizhou.
units.literal: Cui Ning was originally a man of Anping in Bei Prefecture and later moved to Wei Prefecture.

units.zh: 冕被謗，朝廷疑之，遣使者問狀，寧部兵剺耳白其冤，使者以聞。
units.en: When Pei Mian was slandered and the court grew suspicious, an envoy was sent to investigate; Ning's soldiers cut their ears to proclaim Pei's innocence, and the envoy reported back.
units.literal: Mian was slandered and the court suspected him; an envoy was sent to inquire into the matter; Ning's troops slashed their ears and plainly declared his innocence, and the envoy reported upward.

units.zh: 世儒家，而獨喜縱橫事，因落魄，客劍南，以步卒事鮮于仲通。
units.en: Though his family were scholars for generations, he favored political stratagems; down on his luck, he wandered into Jiannan and served Xianyu Zhongtong as a foot soldier.
units.literal: His family for generations were Confucian scholars, yet he alone delighted in coalition diplomacy; because he was down on his luck he sojourned in Jiannan and served Xianyu Zhongtong as an infantryman.

units.zh: 又從李宓討雲南，無功，還成都，行軍司馬崔論悅之，薦為牙將。
units.en: He followed Li Mi's failed Yunnan campaign, returned to Chengdu, won the favor of military secretary Cui Lun, and was made a guard officer.
units.literal: He again followed Li Mi in campaigning against Yunnan without achievement, returned to Chengdu, and Military Affairs Secretary Cui Lun was pleased with him and recommended him as a guard officer.

units.zh: 寧亦還京師，留為折沖郎將。
units.en: Ning too returned to the capital and was kept on as a resolute-assault colonel.
units.literal: Ning also returned to the capital and was retained as a Colonel of the Resolute Assault.

units.zh: 嚴武白寧為利州刺史，既至，賊遁去，由是知名。
units.en: Yan Wu recommended Ning for prefect of Lizhou; on his arrival the bandits dispersed, and he won a name for himself.
units.literal: Yan Wu petitioned that Ning be made Administrator of Li Prefecture; once he arrived the bandits fled, and thereby he became known.

units.zh: 武遂奏為漢州刺史。
units.en: Yan Wu then had him appointed prefect of Hanzhou.
units.literal: Wu thereupon memorialized that he be made Administrator of Han Prefecture.

units.zh: 於是武遣寧將而西，既薄賊城，城皆累石，不得攻，惟東南不合者丈許，諜知之，乃為地道，再宿而拔，拓地數百里。
units.en: Yan Wu sent Ning west; the stone-walled rebel stronghold could not be stormed until spies found a one-zhang gap in the southeast; Ning dug a tunnel, took the city in two nights, and extended Tang control for hundreds of li.
units.literal: Thereupon Wu sent Ning to lead troops west; once he drew near the rebel city, the walls were all piled stone and could not be assaulted; only on the southeast was a gap of about a zhang—spies learned this, and he made a tunnel; in two nights he took it and extended territory for several hundred li.

units.zh: 寶應初，蜀亂，山賊乘險，道不通。
units.en: Early in Baoying, with Shu in turmoil, mountain bandits held the passes and cut the roads.
units.literal: At the beginning of Baoying Shu was in turmoil; mountain bandits exploited the terrain and roads were impassable.

units.zh: 及武為劍南節度使，過州，心欲與俱西，而利非所屬，使寧自為計。
units.en: When Yan Wu became military governor of Jiannan and passed through Lizhou, he wanted Ning to accompany him west, but Lizhou lay outside his circuit, so he told Ning to find his own way.
units.literal: When Wu became Military Governor of Jiannan he passed through the prefecture and wished in his heart to take him west together, but Li was not under his jurisdiction, so he had Ning devise his own plan.

units.zh: 及還，武大悅，裝七寶輿迎入成都，以誇於軍。
units.en: On his return Yan Wu was overjoyed, met him in Chengdu with a jeweled carriage, and paraded the honor before the army.
units.literal: When he returned, Wu was greatly pleased, fitted out a seven-jeweled carriage to welcome him into Chengdu, and displayed this to boast before the army.

units.zh: 歷事崔圓、裴冕。
units.en: He served in turn under Cui Yuan and Pei Mian.
units.literal: He successively served Cui Yuan and Pei Mian.

units.zh: 寧曰：「節度使張獻誠見疑，難輒去。
units.en: Ning said, "Governor Zhang Xiancheng is suspicious of me, so I cannot simply leave.
units.literal: Ning said: "Military Governor Zhang Xiancheng is suspicious of me and it would be hard to leave abruptly.

units.zh: 然獻誠嗜利，若厚賂之，寧可以從大夫矣。」
units.en: But he is greedy; bribe him heavily and I can follow you west."
units.literal: Yet Xiancheng is greedy for profit; if he is richly bribed, I can follow the great officer.

units.zh: 武然之，以奇錦珍貝遺獻誠，且求寧，獻誠果喜，令自移疾去。
units.en: Yan Wu agreed, sent rare silks and jewels to Xiancheng and asked for Ning; delighted, Xiancheng let Ning resign on grounds of illness.
units.literal: Wu approved this, sent rare silks and precious shells to Xiancheng and also requested Ning; Xiancheng was indeed pleased and ordered him to remove himself on grounds of illness.

units.zh: 虜眾驚相謂曰：「寧，神兵也！」
units.en: The enemy cried in alarm, "Ning commands supernatural troops!"
units.literal: The barbarian host cried out to one another in alarm: "Ning is divine troops!"

units.zh: 行軍司馬杜濟，別將郭英幹、郭嘉琳皆請英幹之兄英乂為節度使，寧與其軍亦丐大將王崇俊。
units.en: Du Ji, Guo Yinggan, and Guo Jialin all urged making Yinggan's elder brother Yingyi military governor; Ning and his army asked for the senior general Wang Chongjun instead.
units.literal: Military Affairs Secretary Du Ji, subordinate generals Guo Yinggan and Guo Jialin all requested Yinggan's elder brother Yingyi as Military Governor; Ning and his army also begged for the great general Wang Chongjun.

units.zh: 寧本名旰，至是賜名。
units.en: His original name was Gan; at this point the court granted him the name Ning.
units.literal: Ning's original name was Gan; at this time he was granted the name Ning.

units.zh: 寧方在朝，軍無帥，德宗促寧進鎮。
units.en: With Ning at court and Shu leaderless, Dezong pressed him to return to his command.
units.literal: Ning was then at court and the army had no commander; Emperor Dezong urged Ning to advance and take up his command.

units.zh: 炎業與有嫌，恐已入蜀不可制，即說帝曰：「蜀，天下之奧壤，自寧擅制，朝廷失外府十四年矣。
units.en: Yang Yan, already hostile, feared Ning would become uncontrollable in Shu and told the emperor, "Shu is the empire's richest redoubt; Ning has held it autonomously for fourteen years.
units.literal: Yan had long borne a grudge and feared that once he entered Shu he could not be controlled; he thereupon said to the Emperor: "Shu is the hidden fertile land of the realm; since Ning has ruled it on his own, the court has lost this outer province for fourteen years.

units.zh: 今寧雖來，以全師守蜀，賦稅入天子者與無地同。
units.en: Even now, if he returns with his full army, the court will receive no more revenue than if Shu did not exist.
units.literal: Now though Ning has come, if he guards Shu with his full army, the taxes that enter the Son of Heaven are the same as if there were no territory.

units.zh: 寧本與諸將等夷，獨因叛亂得位，不敢自有，以恩柔煦育，故威令不行。
units.en: Ning had originally been no higher than the other generals. Because he alone had gained his position amid the rebellions, he did not dare assert his own authority; he governed through favors and indulgence, so his commands carried no weight.
units.literal: Ning was originally the equal of other generals and alone gained position through rebellion; he did not dare act on his own authority, and by gentle favor warmed and nurtured them, so his authority and orders did not prevail.

units.zh: 炎曰：「請無歸寧。
units.en: Yan said, "Do not send Ning back.
units.literal: Yan said: "I beg that Ning not be returned.

units.zh: 今朱泚所部范陽勁卒戍近甸，趨與禁兵雜往，舉無不克，因是役得以親兵內其腹中，則蜀將破膽不敢動，然後換授他帥，以收其權，得千里肥饒之地，是謂因小禍受大福也。」
units.en: Zhu Ci's Fanyang veterans garrison the capital approaches; march them with the palace guard and they cannot fail. Use that campaign to plant loyal troops in Ning's rear, terrify Shu into inaction, then replace him and recover a thousand li of rich land—turn a small risk into a great gain."
units.literal: Now the stalwart troops of Fanyang under Zhu Ci garrison the near suburbs; hurry them mixed with the palace guard—nothing undertaken will not succeed; by this campaign we can get trusted troops inside his belly, then Shu will break its courage and not dare move; afterward replace him with another commander to recover his power, and gain a thousand-li of fertile land—this is called receiving great fortune through a small calamity.

units.zh: 遂罷寧西川節度，改兼京畿觀察使、靈州大都督、單於鎮北大都護、朔方節度、鄜坊丹延州都團練觀察等使，托言重臣綏靜北陲，而每道置留後，使得自奏事，杜希全靈州，王翃振武，李建徽鄜州，及戴休顏、杜從政、呂希倩皆炎署置，使伺寧過失。
units.en: Ning was stripped of West River and given nominal commands over the capital region and the northern frontier while Yang Yan installed loyal acting commissioners—Du Xiquan, Wang Hong, Li Jianhui, Dai Xiuyan, Du Congzheng, and Lü Xiqian—to watch his every move.
units.literal: He thereupon removed Ning from West River military governorship and changed him to concurrent Metropolitan Observation Commissioner, Great Governor of Ling Prefecture, Grand Protector of Shanyu and the North, Military Governor of Shuofang, and Training and Observation Commissioner of the prefectures Fu, Fang, Dan, and Yan, on the pretext that a great minister would pacify the northern frontier; yet in each circuit acting commissioners were placed who could memorialize on their own—Du Xiquan at Ling, Wang Hong at Zhenwu, Li Jianhui at Fu, and Dai Xiuyan, Du Congzheng, and Lü Xiqian were all appointed by Yan—to watch for Ning's faults.

units.zh: 寧至夏州，與希倩招党項，降者甚眾。
units.en: At Xiazhou, Ning and Lü Xiqian won over many Tangut tribes.
units.literal: When Ning reached Xia Prefecture he joined with Xiqian in summoning the Tangut; those who surrendered were very many.

units.zh: 炎惡之，即奏希倩無綏邊才，而以神武將軍時常春代之，更拜寧尚書右僕射、知省事，司空如故。
units.en: Yang Yan, alarmed, replaced Xiqian with Shi Changchun and recalled Ning as right vice director while leaving his minister of works title intact.
units.literal: Yan detested this and immediately memorialized that Xiqian lacked talent to pacify the frontier, and had the Shenwu General Shi Changchun replace him; Ning was further appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs directing routine business, with Minister of Works unchanged.

units.zh: 朱泚亂，帝出居奉天，寧後數日至，帝喜甚。
units.en: When Zhu Ci rebelled and the emperor fled to Fengtian, Ning arrived a few days later to the emperor's great relief.
units.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled the Emperor went out to reside at Fengtian; Ning arrived several days later and the Emperor was greatly pleased.

units.zh: 寧謂所親曰：「上聰明，從善如轉規，但為盧杞所惑至此爾。」
units.en: Ning told his intimates, "The emperor is wise and receptive to good counsel, but Lu Qi has led him to this pass."
units.literal: Ning said to those close to him: "The Emperor is intelligent and turns to the good as if revolving a compass, but he has been misled by Lu Qi to reach this point.

units.zh: 杞聞之，思有以構寧於帝。
units.en: Qi heard of this and began plotting to destroy Ning.
units.literal: When Qi heard of it he thought how he might frame Ning before the Emperor.

units.zh: 會王翃赴難時，與寧俱出延平門而西，寧數下馬趨廁，輒迂久。
units.en: During the flight west from Yanping Gate with Wang Hong, Ning kept dismounting for long visits to the privy.
units.literal: It happened that when Wang Hong went to the rescue he and Ning together went out the Yanping Gate westward; Ning repeatedly dismounted and hurried to the privy, always tarrying long.

units.zh: 會泚行反間，而除柳渾為宰相，署寧中書令。
units.en: Zhu Ci spread disinformation, Liu Hun was made chief minister, and Ning was named director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: It happened that Ci carried out a stratagem of alienation, while Liu Hun was appointed chief minister and Ning was commissioned Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 時朔方掌書記康湛為盩厔尉，翃逼湛詐作寧遺泚書獻之，杞遂奏：「寧初無效順心，向聞與賊盟署中書令，今果後至，復得所與賊書，反狀明甚。
units.en: Wang Hong forced Kang Zhan to forge a letter from Ning to Zhu Ci; Qi then memorialized, "Ning had never been loyal, had long been rumored to have accepted a rebel appointment as director of the Secretariat, had arrived late, and now the forged letter proved treason beyond doubt.
units.literal: At that time the Shuofang secretariat clerk Kang Zhan was Assistant Magistrate of Zhouzhi; Hong compelled Zhan to forge a letter from Ning to Ci and presented it; Qi thereupon memorialized: "Ning from the first had no heart of loyal submission; I earlier heard he joined with the rebels in appointing him Director of the Secretariat; now he has indeed arrived late, and again we have obtained the letter he sent the rebels—the signs of rebellion are very clear.

units.zh: 帝命左右扶起之，乃召寧至朝堂，雲使宣慰江淮。
units.en: The emperor had him raised, summoned Ning to court, and pretended to send him to console Jianghuai.
units.literal: The Emperor ordered attendants to raise him up, then summoned Ning to the court hall on the pretext of sending him to console Jianghuai.

units.zh: 俄而中人引寧幕後，使二力士縊殺之，年六十一。
units.en: Eunuchs then led him behind the screen, where two brawny executioners strangled him; he was sixty-one.
units.literal: Before long eunuchs led Ning behind the curtain and had two strongmen strangle him to death; he was sixty-one.

units.zh: 初，命陸贄草制，贄索寧與泚書，將坐其事。
units.en: The emperor first ordered Lu Zhi to draft the edict; Lu Zhi asked for Ning's letter to Zhu Ci, intending to use it as evidence.
units.literal: At first the Emperor ordered Lu Zhi to draft the edict; Zhi demanded Ning's letter to Ci, intending to use it to convict him.

units.zh: 寧死，籍其家，中外冤之。
units.en: After Ning's death his property was confiscated, and the whole court regarded it as a grievous injustice.
units.literal: Ning died, his household property was registered and confiscated, and within and without the court all considered it unjust.

units.zh: 帝乃赦寧親屬，而歸其資雲。
units.en: The emperor then pardoned Ning's kin and restored his family's property.
units.literal: The Emperor thereupon pardoned Ning's kin and returned his assets.

units.zh: 貞元十二年，寧故將夏綏銀節度使韓潭請以所加禮部尚書雪寧罪，有詔聽其家收葬。
units.en: In 796, Han Tan, Ning's former subordinate and military governor of Xia-Sui-Yin, offered to relinquish his newly granted post of Minister of Rites in exchange for clearing Ning's name; the court then allowed Ning's family to recover and bury his body.
units.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhenyuan, Ning's former officer Han Tan, Military Governor of Xia, Sui, and Yin, requested to clear Ning's guilt with the additionally granted post of Minister of Rites; an edict permitted his family to collect the body for burial.

units.zh: 始，寧入朝，留其弟寬守成都，楊子琳乘間起瀘州，以精騎數千襲據其城。
units.en: When Ning went to court he left his brother Kuan in Chengdu; Yang Zilin seized the moment, marched from Luzhou with thousands of elite horsemen, and took the city by surprise.
units.literal: At the beginning, when Ning entered court he left his younger brother Kuan to guard Chengdu; Yang Zilin seized the opportunity to rise from Lu Prefecture and with several thousand elite horsemen surprised and seized the city.

units.zh: 寬戰力屈，寧妾任素驍果，即出家財十萬募勇士，得千人，設部隊，自將以進。
units.en: Kuan was beaten back, but Ning's concubine Lady Ren, who was known for her courage and resolve, spent one hundred thousand cash of her own to raise a thousand warriors, formed them into units, and led the counterattack herself.
units.literal: Kuan's strength in battle was exhausted. Ning's concubine, Lady Ren, had always been bold and resolute; she immediately contributed one hundred thousand in family wealth, recruited a thousand brave men, organized them into units, and personally led them forward.

units.zh: 寧季弟密，密子繪，俱以文辭稱。
units.en: Ning's youngest brother Mi and Mi's son Hui were both noted for their literary talent.
units.literal: Ning's youngest younger brother Mi, and Mi's son Hui, were both famed for literary composition.

units.zh: 判度支盧坦、兵部尚書判戶部事王紹、鹽鐵使王播請許商人於戶部、度支、鹽鐵三司飛錢，每千錢增給百錢，然商人無至者。
units.en: Lu Tan, Wang Shao, and Wang Bo proposed state-sponsored flying money through the three fiscal offices with a hundred-cash premium per thousand—but no merchants used it.
units.literal: Acting Expenditure Commissioner Lu Tan, Minister of War acting for the Ministry of Revenue Wang Shao, and Salt Commissioner Wang Bo requested allowing merchants flying money at the three offices of Revenue, Expenditure, and Salt and Iron, adding one hundred cash per thousand; yet no merchants came.

units.zh: 復許與商人敵貫而易之，然錢重帛輕如故。
units.en: They again allowed merchants to exchange at par, yet coin remained scarce and silk cheap as before.
units.literal: They again allowed merchants to exchange at par, yet coin remained heavy and silk light as before.

units.zh: 自京師禁飛錢，家有滯藏，物價寖輕。
units.en: After the capital banned flying money, hoarded coin sat idle and prices gradually fell.
units.literal: Since the capital forbade flying money, households had stagnant hoards and prices gradually fell.

units.zh: 鴻漸與六城水運使魏少遊、節度判官崔漪、支度判官盧簡金、關內鹽池判官李涵謀曰：「今胡羯亂常，二京陷沒，主上南幸於巴蜀，皇太子理兵於平涼。
units.en: Hongjian conferred with Wei Shaoyou, commissioner for the Six Cities water transport, military governor's aide Cui Yi, supplies aide Lu Jianjin, and Guannei salt-pond aide Li Han. He said, "The barbarian rebels have thrown the realm into chaos. Both capitals have fallen. The emperor has fled south to Ba-Shu, and the crown prince is gathering troops at Pingliang.
units.literal: Hongjian plotted with Wei Shaoyou, commissioner for the Six Cities water transport, the military governor's aide Cui Yi, the supplies aide Lu Jianjin, and the Guannei salt-pond aide Li Han, saying, "Now the barbarian rebels have thrown the realm into chaos; the two capitals have fallen; the sovereign has toured south to Ba-Shu, and the Crown Prince is organizing troops at Pingliang.

units.zh: 鴻漸即日草箋具陳兵馬招集之勢，錄軍資、器械、倉儲、庫物之數，令李涵賫赴平涼，肅宗大悅。
units.en: That same day Hongjian drafted a detailed report on troop strength and listed all military funds, weapons, and stores, sending Li Han to Pingliang with it. Suzong was delighted.
units.literal: That same day Hongjian drafted a memorial fully setting forth the situation for gathering troops and horses, recorded the numbers of military funds, weapons, granaries, and storehouse goods, and had Li Han carry it to Pingliang; Suzong was greatly pleased.

units.zh: 李巽為諸道轉運、鹽鐵使，以堰埭歸鹽鐵使，罷其增置者。
units.en: Li Xun as circuit transport and salt-and-iron commissioner returned the dams to salt-and-iron control and abolished Li Qi's extra taxes.
units.literal: Li Xun served as circuit transport and salt-and-iron commissioner, returned dams and weirs to the salt-and-iron office, and abolished the added levies.

units.zh: 自劉晏後，江淮米至渭橋寖減矣，至巽乃復如晏之多。
units.en: After Liu Yan, Jiang-Huai grain to Wei Bridge had steadily fallen; under Li Xun it recovered to Yan's levels.
units.literal: After Liu Yan, Jiang-Huai rice reaching Wei Bridge had gradually diminished; only with Xun did it again reach Yan's volume.

units.zh: 十月，與朔方節度使司徒郭子儀、河東節度使太尉李光弼等九節度同圍安慶緒於相州。
units.en: In the tenth month he joined Shuofang governor Guo Ziyi, Hedong governor Li Guangbi, and eight other commanders in besieging An Qingxu at Xiangzhou.
units.literal: In the tenth month, together with the Shuofang military governor and Minister of Works Guo Ziyi, the Hedong military governor and Grand Marshal Li Guangbi, and eight other frontier commands, he jointly besieged An Qingxu at Xiangzhou.

units.zh: 五日，至新鄭縣，聞郭子儀已整眾屯谷水，李光弼還太原，炅憂懼，仰藥而卒。
units.en: On the fifth he reached Xinzheng and learned that Guo Ziyi had regrouped at Gushui while Li Guangbi had gone back to Taiyuan. In fear and despair Jiong took poison and died.
units.literal: On the fifth day, reaching Xinzheng County, he heard that Guo Ziyi had already reassembled his force at Gushui and Li Guangbi had returned to Taiyuan; Jiong, anxious and afraid, took poison and died.

units.zh: ○苗晉卿裴冕裴遵慶子向向子寅寅子樞=苗晉卿=苗晉卿，上黨壺關人。
units.en: This section covers Miao Jinqing, Pei Mian, and Pei Zunqing, together with Pei Xiang, Xiang's son Yin, and Yin's son Shu. Miao Jinqing was from Huguan in Shangdang.
units.literal: [Section:] Miao Jinqing, Pei Mian, Pei Zunqing, his son Xiang, Xiang's son Yin, Yin's son Shu. = Miao Jinqing = Miao Jinqing was a native of Huguan in Shangdang.

units.zh: 其後諸道鹽鐵、轉運使張滂復置江淮巡院。
units.en: Later circuit transport commissioner Zhang Pang restored the Jiang-Huai patrol office.
units.literal: Afterward circuit salt-and-iron and transport commissioner Zhang Pang restored the Jiang-Huai patrol office.

units.zh: 李靈曜反於汴州，鎰訓練鄉兵，嚴守禦之備，詔書褒異，加侍御史、沿淮鎮守使。
units.en: When Li Lingyao rebelled at Bianzhou, Zhang Yi trained local militia and rigorously prepared the defenses. An imperial edict singled him out for praise and added the posts of attendant censor and commissioner for defense along the Huai.
units.literal: When Li Lingyao rebelled at Bianzhou, Yi trained local militia and strictly prepared defenses; an imperial edict praised him with distinction and added the posts of attendant censor and commissioner for defense along the Huai.
